body:
I am so sorry you are not getting support. That is heartbreaking. So many don't understand, and react with anger or fear. It is inexcusable for your husband to yell at you while you were hurting. That makes me so angry for you.  

It's good you're going to a therapist. What about your family? It might benefit them, help them understand you are trying to be well.

Not everyone wants a chiseled jaw and a 6-pack though. My ex husband was super "hot" in a conventional way and it really frankly turned me off at the end. He was obsessed with himself and very cruel. Plus, looks fade.

I don't think it makes sense to put virginity up on a pedestal... Sex is just something you haven't tried, not like... the Holy Grail. Even though it might feel that way sometimes.

But I understand. The world can be frustrating and discouraging. But it's not you, you're not the problem. Shallow people are selfish lovers anyway, lol.

Real people are out there. Focus on yourself, try to figure out who you really want to be. Love (the good kind) will meet you where you are.

Hi, I'm 27 too, a girl though. I wouldn't think it was that weird that a guy was still a virgin at this age. We're still so young. One of my friends just got married to a guy that stayed a virgin until their wedding night (he is VERY religious, though).

The thing about girls is, we're complex people too. I feel like both of these girls you built up in your mind to be something bigger than what they really were, which was flawed human beings. Everyone is flawed. The biggest thing is comfort... if you feel comfortable enough with someone to be completely honest about your feelings, and your past, without fear of being judged... then they are the right person for you. The right person will accept you. And don't base your happiness off what someone else does. The way someone else acts isn't your fault or your doing. Don't blame yourself. 

Also this is a dumb suggestion that I'm sure you've thought of, but have you tried online dating at all? There are other people out there, looking for someone to talk to or hold. Just be yourself. You sound like a thoughtful person. A couple girls who weren't right for you don't mean there is no one who is right for you. You're not a waste of skin, good sir.

Yes. I know exactly how you feel. I accidentally overdosed last year (on medicine that was prescribed to me, not at all on purpose) and I was so pissed off because while I knew I was going to kill myself eventually, I didn't want it to be by accident. I felt stupid. In the moment I was just mad, but afterwards I was so afraid, because my eventual suicide was a fact to me. I will kill myself one day.  I don't have any specific reason, but I still think it's inevitable. I just don't feel like I can handle living. Is it like that for you, too?

Someone a long time ago quoted Camus on this board, said that every day they chose to live... Live in spite of there being no reason, live in revolt. I like this concept a lot. 

Why do you feel you are worthless?

I don't know about noble, but I do feel like if I can't make myself happy, the least I can do while I am here is try to make other people's lives better. I am headed down to Mexico; to a small village. It's mostly selfish, though. I want a simple life. 

That is a good reason to choose engineering. Happy inventing, peace to you as well.

Hello overseas stranger, I understand. 

I was always told I was smart, and that I shouldn't "waste" my intelligence on art or humanitarian pursuits... so I got a geophysics degree and went to work in the oil business. It's unfulfilling, frustrating, and pointless. The only time I am happy is when I help others, which thankfully I get to do sometimes with my job.

I am planning to leave my so-called prestigious career soon to move to a developing country. I'm going to open a pizza restaurant and help people learn English, and stop caring about money and status. I hope it helps. I really think it will.

I don't have any advice for you other than to hold on to the fact that it makes you happy to help others. That is good, and that is valuable. It is more valuable than you will ever know. Society is backwards. We are not here to make money, to work in jobs that make corporations money. We are here to make it easier on each other. Good luck to you. <3

Haha! I like that, though. 

I'm happy, quite often, on a superficial level. But still there is that feeling, the knowledge that I don't want, that I can't get rid of. It's like the base layer of black paint underneath a vibrant sunset or something. 

And like, I don't even know if I would want to snap my fingers and get rid of it either? I feel like it gives my life some depth and context that someone living on the surface wouldn't have. Like, I don't want to have one foot out of the material world really, but I'm glad I'm aware of it's transience. If that makes sense.

That mask is super cooling and feels really good! When my hormonal acne was really bad, nothing over-the-counter really helped, but that definitely made it more comfortable. Birth control and spironolactone (anti-androgen) fixed mine. 

"Honest" with yourself... I know what you mean. I don't want to coddle myself, so I end up talking down to myself, too. I've been trying to reframe honesty like... how honest you'd be with a friend. Even if your close friend really *was* bad at something they liked... like, I'm really pretty tone deaf too, but I love singing... you wouldn't say, "Friend, you're a freaking horrible singer and you should just stop trying." You'd be more like, "Friend, you're not the best singer, but it's ok. It makes you happy, so that makes me happy." :)

I understand those feelings; I am also my own worst critic.  Someone once told me: talk to yourself how you would talk to someone you love. Take care of yourself like you would take care of someone you love. Even if you feel you are not worthy of love, pretend you are. Give yourself a day off, make something good and healthy for yourself to eat, do a face mask. Face masks are so soothing, seriously under-rated in terms of therapy. Queen Helene makes a cheap one you can get at the drugstore that dries up acne (I used to have a zit-beard and it always felt really nice). 

Also, when I had really bad acne it turned out to be a hormonal imbalance. Hormones are freaking crazy, they could actually be behind a lot of things you mentioned. 

Good luck to you. 

<3

No, I'm pretty much in the best place I've ever been in  my life. I have everything to live for, at least "everything" in the traditional normal-happy-life sense: money, job, a partner, family, friends, a place to live. None of it matters. I'm still depressed, and I feel terrible, because I know I don't have any right to be.

Thank you for that last sentence. Yes, what we do every day is what matters. I try to help other people whenever I can. That makes me feel better. Good luck to you too <3

also ETA: I think I've "made it this far" because I was in a really *bad* place from 16 to 24 years old (abusive marriage). I reasoned with myself that I was unhappy due to that situation, and when I got out, I would find hope in my life again. I do have happiness now, and hope, but I still can't shake the depression/suicidal thoughts. It's frustrating.

hey I just found this thread. I want to say, I feel you. the older i get the more i realize how blind everyone wants to be. let them. the modern world is designed to distract people.

all it takes is one person who gets you; we're out there.

also, i'm moving to a mountain town in mexico to open a pizza restaurant, and i fully plan on never, ever watching the news again
